# PDF fixture licenses

Each fixture under `tests/fixtures/pdfs/` is recorded here with its provenance
and license. Fixtures land in phase 2 (`digital-clean/*.pdf`), phase 3
(`digital-broken/*.pdf`), phase 4 (`image-scan/*.pdf`), and phase 9 (full
benchmark corpus including `mixed/` and `edge/`).

| Fixture | Phase added | Source | License |
|---|---|---|---|
| `digital-clean/lorem-ar-2col.pdf` | 2 | Generated by `tools/generate_fixtures.py` (reportlab + Helvetica). ASCII content, two pages. | MIT (project-owned) |
| `digital-clean/lorem-ar-en-mixed.pdf` | 2 | Generated by `tools/generate_fixtures.py` (reportlab + Helvetica). ASCII content mixing two paragraphs. | MIT (project-owned) |
| `digital-clean/lorem-ar-table.pdf` | 2 | Generated by `tools/generate_fixtures.py` (reportlab + Helvetica). One page with a 3-by-3 grid table. | MIT (project-owned) |
| `digital-clean/lorem-ar-real.pdf` | 2 | Generated by `tools/generate_fixtures.py` (reportlab + a system Noto / DejaVu Arabic-capable TTF). One page carrying real Arabic codepoints in the text layer. The visual rendering is not bidi-shaped because we deliberately avoid pulling in `arabic_reshaper` / `python-bidi` (their licenses do not match the project's allow-list) — the test layer's job is to exercise Unicode plumbing, not to be visually correct. Phase 9 enriches the corpus with bidi-shaped Arabic. | MIT (project-owned generated artefact; embedded font remains under the system font's own license — Noto OFL or DejaVu Bitstream Vera; both permit subset embedding by `reportlab`). |

Phase 9 will enrich this corpus with real, license-clean Arabic-content PDFs
(InDesign / LaTeX-bidi / Wikisource provenance) under `digital-clean/`,
`digital-broken/`, `image-scan/`, `mixed/`, and `edge/`. Until then the
phase-2 fixtures exist to exercise the extractor's geometry and Unicode
plumbing — not to be a realistic Arabic typesetting benchmark.

The license-audit harness is permissive about fixture content (it reads only
`models.toml` and the live distribution set) — fixture licensing is enforced
manually at PR-review time, not in CI.
